bullets.title: Broad Market Bounces Hard After Worst Semis Week Since 2011
bullets.body: S&P futures opened +2.5-2.9% and Nasdaq 100 futures +3.1-3.5% Monday morning after a brutal week that saw the S&P 500 fall ~8.6-9.3%, NDX -10-11%, and SOX -17% — the worst week for semis since September 2011 and bottom-5 NDX week in 20 years. The bounce is led by the AI trade, with NVDA +7-9%, ARM +9%, and SNOW +16% pre-market. VIX hit 36 (matching Dec 2018) and hedge fund net leverage fell to ~41%, near multi-year lows.

bullets.title: Trump/Bessent Soften on Jensen, No New China Chip Restrictions — Key Catalyst for Bounce
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent left the door open to Jensen Huang's return as NVDA CEO and signaled no further chip export restrictions to China are needed; Trump separately said Jensen should apologize and return. This reversal is cited across sources as a primary catalyst for Monday's AI trade bounce, partially relieving the SEC accounting probe and China spy scandal overhangs that drove last week's selloff.

bullets.title: Multiple Strategists Call 'Fat Pitch' Valuation: S&P at 16.4x vs ~19x Fair Value
bullets.body: MS CIO Mike Wilson and JPM both flag S&P 500 at 16.4x forward EPS — roughly 3 multiple turns below MS's 19.0-19.6x fair value estimate — with the NDX below COVID trough valuations at 17x and SOX at 12-13x. Market is pricing -6% EPS growth in 2027 vs MS's +14% and Street's +17% forecasts. JPM maintains an $8,000 year-end S&P target with FY27 EPS of $420. Both recommend gradual exposure build in quality names with patience, as HF capitulation signal is not yet confirmed (positioning at 13th percentile since 2015).

bullets.title: Fed Expected to Hike Dec & March; Market Pricing Too Hawkish vs Eventual Path
bullets.body: JPM and MS both expect 25bp Fed hikes in December and March, bringing the target to 4.50-4.75%, then a hold through 2027. However, MS argues financial conditions are already tighter than 2018/2022 levels and the market is pricing too hawkish a path — the Fed should deliver a more measured December message. The 10-year yield is around 4.93-4.94%, with the 5-year down ~25bp over the prior week.

bullets.title: UBS Cuts Semi Data Center Estimates 10%/20% in C2027/C2028 on ~25% Supply Overbuild
bullets.body: UBS's Tim Arcuri is cutting data center revenue estimates ~10% in C2027E and ~20% in C2028E across semiconductor coverage, citing a ~25% gap between compute build plans (~51GW) and high-confidence powered shell capacity (~38GW) for 2027. Memory downturn now pulled forward into C2028. SOX NTM P/E is now only 10-15% above 2018 and post-COVID trough levels, suggesting a potential tactical bottom. Token demand remains strong; the constraint is on the supply side from permitting.

bullets.title: AI Capex Mid-Cycle Thesis: Growth Slows Sharply in 2027-28; Non-AI Economy Absorbs Slack
bullets.body: Multiple sources (Nancy Lazar, JPM) converge on AI capex being mid-cycle, not early-cycle. JPM models total AI capex at $1.4T in 2027 (nearly doubling 2026) then decelerating sharply in 2028+, with 23GW under construction and 97GW committed globally. Lazar notes Mag-8/Neocloud 2027 capex plans slowing sharply and 2028 showing a 'very sharp slowdown' (-1.3ppts GDP impulse). Data centers planned but not started are falling, indicating fewer new projects entering construction. Non-AI capex broadening and lagged Fed easing are expected to support ~6% nominal GDP growth in 2027 despite the AI deceleration.

bullets.title: AI Capex Financing Stress: Debt Caps Force $2.9T Equity Requirement; Power Remains Bottleneck
bullets.body: JPM estimates 2026 AI infrastructure financing at $476B (primarily investment-grade bonds), with 2027 requiring $450B+ in public high-grade debt. Debt financing constraints are tightening — loan-to-cost ratios expected to decline from 70-95% to ~60% — requiring $2.9T cumulative equity investment over five years, equating to ~55% of hyperscaler base-case operating cash flow. Power bottlenecks persist; PJM and ERCOT markets are struggling with data center load requests, and BTM solutions face natural gas pipeline constraints.

bullets.title: Hyperscalers Face Investor Pressure on AI ROI Clarity; AMZN and UBER Flagged as Best Risk/Reward
bullets.body: Goldman flags that aggregate capex across AMZN, GOOGL, META, and SPCX exceeded $170B in Q3 alone, with hyperscalers increasingly reliant on outside capital. Investors are demanding clearer strategic roadmaps on AI right-to-win, platform initiatives at scale, and investment cycle duration. GS highlights AMZN (Buy, $370 PT; AWS 39% growth expected to accelerate 40%+ in 2027/28) and UBER as particularly compelling risk/rewards. META cut its own PT by MS to $720 (from $820) after raising 2027 opex to $227B on $23B incremental cloud spend.

bullets.title: NVDA Faces Multi-Front Overhang: SEC Probe, China Spy Scandal, Export Compliance, Supplier Halts
bullets.body: NVDA is down ~32-48% from recent highs with overlapping headwinds: SEC investigating accounting practices, DNI confirmed a probe into an alleged Chinese spy who had an affair with Jensen Huang, Singapore (~50% of international revenue) flagged as export compliance risk, and Southeast Asia server suppliers halting shipments. JPM estimates Singapore represents ~21.7% of total NVDA revenue, making export restriction enforcement a material financial risk.

bullets.title: CRWD Acquires Zscaler for $43.9B All-Stock; Largest Security Deal Ever
bullets.body: CrowdStrike is acquiring Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at $43.9B at 1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share (~34% premium to ZS's Nov 20 close), creating a broader cyber platform spanning endpoint, identity, SIEM, cloud, SASE, and network security. CRWD -9% on deal announcement; ZS ARR grew +21% y/y to $3.88B in Q1 with NN ARR of $419M beating by $75M. UBS estimates $1B annualized revenue synergies and $500M cost synergies. Jay Chaudhry (~34% of ZS shares) committed to vote for the deal; close expected H2 FY28.

bullets.title: Cybersecurity Sector Outperforms Amid M&A Wave; PANW Also Acquiring Applied Compute for $4.5B
bullets.body: Security sector outperformed software and S&P 500 last week (+1.8% vs IGV -9.4%). Beyond CRWD/ZS, PANW beat F1Q27 revenue by $139M with NGS ARR beating by ~$180M and acquiring Applied Compute for $4.5B in all-stock. PANW is also reportedly in talks for Israeli Terra Security at $500M+. OpenAI's Brockman flagged cybersecurity as a business already 'growing extremely rapidly' and potentially larger than coding for AI models.

bullets.title: Memory Cycle: DRAM +35% ASP in 2027 on HBM Strength; NAND Cut to +25% on Soft Consumer
bullets.body: Citi raises 2027E DRAM contract ASP growth to +35% YoY (from +23%) driven by ~100% HBM ASP hike and resilient server DRAM. Goldman similarly constructive on DRAM: +32% pricing in 2027 with HBM TAM raised to $200B/$237B in 2027/28. NAND is the offset — Citi cuts 2027 NAND ASP growth to +25% from +45% on soft consumer demand and slowing China eSSD. UBS pulls the memory downturn into C2028E from prior C2029E. JPM spot data shows DDR5 +84% y/y; NAND -15% m/m.

bullets.title: Trump Threatens Tax on US Companies Building AI Data Centers Abroad; Geopolitical AI Sovereignty Accelerating
bullets.body: Trump announced a 'tremendous tax' on US data center companies that develop AI campuses outside the country, reinforcing geopolitical constraints on building abroad. BIS remote-access rules on AI compute came in more restrictive than expected, impacting ASEAN project conversions. AI competition is increasingly framed as geopolitical, with governments prioritizing digital sovereignty — Alphabet's Ruth Porat flagged ~€1T in potential European sovereign cloud benefits over the next decade.

bullets.title: SOX Tactical Bottom Signal Emerging but HF Capitulation Not Yet Complete
bullets.body: SOX NTM P/E is 10-15% above 2018 and post-COVID troughs. VIX crossed 30 for the first time since March 2026 — historically a positive signal at T+30 and T+90. HF net leverage at 41% (near Dec 2018 lows), but HF capitulation signal is not yet confirmed with positioning at the 13th percentile since 2015. Retail flows are a headwind: largest Tech ETF liquidation on record occurred last week. CTAs reduced risk but incremental selling pressure may remain.

bullets.title: ORCL OpenAI Infrastructure Deal Fully Funded; FCF Positive H2 FY28, Self-Funded FY29
bullets.body: Oracle secured all $20B in financing required for the OpenAI contract (representing ~50% of existing RPO), with vendor financing locked across a diverse supplier base. The deal is structured as cost-plus with ~35% gross margins and ~30% operating margins. Oracle reaffirmed guidance: positive FCF in 2H FY28 and $30B+ FCF in FY29, with self-funded growth beginning FY29. Abilene campus is nearly complete and Shackelford campus is fully permitted.

bullets.title: AI Capex Unit Growth Slowing in Real Terms Despite Nominal Strength — Supply Chain Signals
bullets.body: Nancy Lazar points to Korea/Taiwan data confirming slowing real AI capex growth: Korea semi export confidence declined sharply, global PMIs for computing equipment new orders shifted down, and World Semiconductor Trade Statistics show much nominal growth is price inflation rather than real volume. Data centers planned but not started are falling. Meanwhile, JPM's DC tracker shows AI usage accelerating +79% m/m with 54x y/y token growth, but spending growth moderated to +8% m/m as model mix shifts to lower-priced open-weight models.

bullets.title: Eurozone PMI Stable at 51.7 but Core Divergence Widens: Germany 55.0 vs France 46.2
bullets.body: Euro area composite PMI held at 51.7 in November, consistent with ~1.3% annualized GDP growth, but Germany surged to 55.0 (2.2% ar growth, boosted by fiscal easing) while France stagnated at 46.2. Inflationary pressures faded with input/output prices dropping. UK flash PMI fell 0.6pts to 52.3 with employment declining nearly 2pts to 48.5, though future output hit its highest level since February at 69.0.

bullets.title: AI Software Sentiment Bottoming; Infrastructure Positive, Apps Skittish, Cyber Tied to Semis
bullets.body: JPM's tech sentiment monitor shows internet sentiment has bottomed and is on the upswing post mini-market crash. Software sentiment is worsening in Cyber (trading with semis), broadly positive in infrastructure, and skittish in applications. Citi's Cloud Forum framework favors AI infrastructure/data winners (MSFT, MDB, SNOW, PLTR) over incumbents (CRM, ADBE, HUBS) as enterprises shift from AI experimentation to production deployment cost/performance requirements.

bullets.title: MRVL PT Slashed to $200 from $350 as UBS Cuts C2028E Revenue 20% on DC Constraints
bullets.body: UBS cuts MRVL C2027E revenue from $20.1B to $18.1B and C2028E from $33.1B to $26.5B on data center power/land constraints, reducing the PT from $350 to $200 at 20x C2028E EPS. The LITE acquisition faces skepticism as LITE is sold out through C2029 and investors question whether MRVL is buying at peak optical scarcity. Near-term estimates for the Oct quarter ($3.2B/$1.10) are maintained.

bullets.title: High-Yield Stress Building: Spreads Widened to 347bp; $298B Maturity Wall in 2028
bullets.body: High-yield spreads widened ~320bp to 347bp last week, confirming equity weakness. JPM flags a $298B HY maturity wall in 2028 and $484B in 2029 — the next three years represent a record 24% of HY outstanding. Record AI infrastructure borrowing has boosted credit profits but is now under pressure from higher rates and slowing issuance. Morgan Stanley credit indices also weakened sharply with Xover widening 30bp on the week.
